answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust is a signal propagated by bounded-length random walks: transition mass reaching a candidate is discounted by path length and normalized by trusted conductance. A sybil cluster may amplify internal links but, lacking external attestations, forms a sparse cut with low conductance. Cheeger-style escape bounds and min-cut transitivity limits therefore cap its aggregate voting weight, whether identities are labeled sparrow or summit.
